checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the image is a tight head-and-shoulders crop, rendering most body and limb checkpoints untestable. The verdicts for visible features (face, fur, eyes) are accurate. The Router was not too lenient; it appropriately marked occluded or out-of-frame features as untestable rather than assuming presence.
artifact_review: The Router identified two key artifacts: texture anomaly (haloing) and structural collapse (foreground object). I agree with these findings. The 'structural_collapse' of the foreground bar is significant because it lacks logical termination and consistent width, a common AI artifact in depth-of-field simulations. The 'texture_anomaly' is subtle but present at the hair-background boundary. The animal_pose_auditor's high risk level (65% low-confidence keypoints) supports the suspicion of structural ambiguity in the shoulders/limbs, even if visually obscured by fur/cropping. The topology_boundary_auditor confirmed the foreground object is a single mask but did not rule out the internal structural inconsistency noted by the Router.
alignment_reasoning: The fine_grained_classifier strongly confirms the class (orangutan) with high confidence (logit 7.91 vs 3.15 for next best). Visible anatomical features (cheek pads, eyes, fur) are highly accurate and consistent with the taxonomy. The score is slightly below 5.0 due to the inability to verify full-body proportions and the slight uncertainty in the shoulder region indicated by the pose auditor.
artifact_reasoning: The image suffers from minor but noticeable generative artifacts. The foreground blur object is structurally nonsensical (inconsistent width, no termination), which disrupts the scene's physical plausibility. There is slight haloing around the fur edges. While the main subject is clean, these environmental/depth artifacts prevent a perfect score. The pose auditor's low confidence in the limbs/shoulders further suggests underlying structural weakness in those occluded areas.
